Part I: Enteral nutrition
Introduction
Enteral nutrition (EN) is the modality of feeding via the gastrointestinal (GI) tract when one cannot sustain or progress their nutri-
tional needs orally. Feeding is delivered directly into the GI tract for absorption of nutrients, ﬂuid, electrolytes, and vitamins.
EN dates back a few thousand years, notably 100 BC when barley and wheat were provided via rectal feeds in patients who were
not capable of eating orally (Vassilyadi et al., 2013; Dudrick and Palesty, 2011). It wasn’t until 1598 that Capivacceus used a hollow
tube placed in the esophagus to deliver liquid nutrients (Dudrick and Palesty, 2011) and Hunter in 1790 (Vassilyadi et al., 2013;
